definition: Running models on phones, browsers, and embedded hardware (quantized SLMs, llama.cpp/MLX/NPU runtimes) for privacy, latency, and offline operation.
details: Running models on phones, browsers, and embedded hardware (quantized SLMs, llama.cpp/MLX/NPU runtimes) for privacy, latency, and offline operation. The counterweight to cloud centralization, and the deployment target that makes quantization and distillation commercially decisive.

explainer.lead: On-device inference runs models on phones, browsers, and embedded hardware, using quantized small language models and runtimes such as llama.cpp, MLX, and NPUs. It matters for privacy, latency, and offline operation, and is the counterweight to cloud centralization.

tiers.eli5: Like doing the maths in your own head instead of sending the question away and waiting for an answer.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers deploy quantized small language models through on-device runtimes to keep data local and responses fast without a network. It is also the deployment target that makes quantization and distillation commercially decisive.
tiers.paperLevel: No formula; the defining constraints are on-device execution with quantized models and runtimes such as llama.cpp, MLX, and NPUs, motivated by privacy, latency, and offline operation.

explainer.example: A phone app runs a quantized small language model locally, so user text never leaves the device and works without connectivity.
